subject: Post-call: Model fit & benchmark next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & benchmark next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Recap from the call
- Primary use case: multi-turn customer support summarization + routing and short action extraction (~1-4 turns, average input length ~120 tokens).
- Success criteria: >95% intent-routing accuracy for top-1, and average latency <120ms p90 for typical prompt sizes.

2) Recommended models to evaluate (based on the workload you described)
- redwood-7b-instruct (baseline, higher quality)
- redwood-7b-quant (4-bit quantized variant, lower cost, slightly lower quality in some long-context cases)

3) Attached / links
- Attached: acme_benchmark_results.csv (sample CSV showing how we format TPS/latency buckets for a small pilot)
- Attached: redwood_perf_profile.pdf (Redwood-verified performance profile for the models above)
- Perf profile link: https://console.redwood.ai/accounts/acme/perf-profiles/redwood-verified-7b

4) Proposed benchmark plan
- You share a sample prompt set (10-20 real customer examples) and expected labels; we run a 24-hour benchmark on our Dedicated infra and return TPS, p50/p90/p99 latency, cost estimate, and quality metrics (accuracy/F1 on your labels).
- If you'd like, we can also run a head-to-head between the two recommended model variants.

5) Next steps
- Could you share 10 representative prompt examples and one example of expected label/output by EOD Thursday?
- We will schedule the benchmark for the following week once we have the prompts and access details.

A couple of quick notes on quality regressions: we will include checkpointed outputs for the prompt set so you can review specific failure modes. If you have a small evaluation harness (pytest-like or a spreadsheet), we can run that as part of the benchmark.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up if you prefer a walkthrough.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com

Attachment: acme_benchmark_results.csv (csv, 12 KB)
Attachment: redwood_perf_profile.pdf (pdf, 220 KB)

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmeinc.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & benchmark next steps

Thanks Alex — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few questions before we send prompts over:

- For the latency numbers in the perf profile: are the p50/p90/p99 numbers measured at 1) cold start or 2) warmed KV cache? Our production pattern will have a mix, but most requests will benefit from warm cache.
- For throughput: what TPS should we expect for short prompts (~120 tokens) on the redwood-7b-quant profile? Any guidance on batching that impacts latency tradeoffs?
- On quality regressions: can you point me to an example of a short prompt where the quantized variant trips up versus the full baseline? That helps us evaluate the risk.

We can share 15 prompts by Thursday. Also, do you need an NDA or can we share a de-identified extract?

—Sam
Sam Jenkins
Senior Engineering Manager, Acme Inc.
sam.jenkins@acmeinc.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & benchmark next steps

Hi Sam — thanks for the questions. Short answers below, plus details in the attached perf profile PDF.

- Cache state: the perf profile numbers are reported for warmed KV cache (steady-state). We also include cold-start percentiles in the full report if you need them. The p50/p90/p99 in the attached PDF are steady-state numbers measured during an extended run.

- Expected TPS for short prompts (~120 tokens) on redwood-7b-quant: ~45-60 TPS per GPU (conservative), depending on batch sizing. With continuous batching tuned for latency SLOs our tests show ~50 TPS with p90 latency ~95ms. The non-quantized redwood-7b-instruct is ~25-35 TPS with p90 ~120-150ms for the same prompt distribution. These are representative numbers from our Dedicated infastructure profiles; we'll provide exact numbers once we run your prompts.

- Quality regression example: in our eval prompt sets we sometimes see the 4-bit quantized variant collapse on long, multi-step extraction prompts (loss of subtle token-level choices). For short extraction/intent tasks you should expect parity in most cases, but we'll include side-by-side diff outputs for any failures. Example (excerpt):

On Mon, Mar 29, 2026 at 10:05 AM Example User <user@example.com> wrote:
> Prompt: "Extract customer intent and timestamp from the message below"
> Input: "Hi — I had an issue on 3/12, please escalate"
> Expected: {intent: \"escalate\", date: \"2026-03-12\"} 
>
> redwood-7b-instruct: correct
> redwood-7b-quant: missed the date field in 2/50 runs

We'll flag these examples in the benchmark output so you can decide whether the cost tradeoff is worth it.

- NDA: de-identified extracts are fine for an initial run; if we need raw PII data later we can sign an NDA.

Next steps: please send the 15 prompts + expected outputs to this thread (de-identified). We'll queue a 24-48 hour benchmark on Dedicated infra and share the perf report, CSV, and model output diffs. I'll also log the HubSpot deal: https://crm.redwood.ai/deals/ACME-2026-042

Best,
Alex

Attachment: redwood_perf_profile.pdf (pdf, 220 KB)
